evidence: Mechanism confirmed in the frozen tree. The inbox dedupe (products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1202-1221) filters head_sha=H, excludes SUPERSEDED and FAILED, then orders by -created_at and returns the first row, so any older non-failed run at H wins over a newer FAILED one and the task returns 'already_reviewed' (tasks.py:1211-1221) without creating a replacement. A COMPLETED and a later FAILED run at the same head can coexist through production paths: COMPLETED is terminal (facade/enums.py:31-33), so _supersede_prior_runs (tasks.py:415-433) never touches run A; a webhook 'reopened' (in _HEAD_CHANGING_ACTIONS, tasks.py:49) or a base retarget ('edited' with changes.base, tasks.py:835) on a bot-authored self-driving PR passes _inbox_rereview_carve_out (tasks.py:167-216, tested at tests/test_tasks.py:762-795) and creates run B at the payload's unchanged head (tasks.py:1055-1063; the retarget test at test_tasks.py:520-556 asserts a fresh same-head run). B's workflow first voids EVERY standing approval, same-head included (temporal/activities.py:266-290, current_head_sha=''), and a retarget additionally dismisses at every head before that (tasks.py:441-472). The sandbox activity gets one attempt (temporal/constants.py:81) and the workflow itself one attempt (temporal/client.py, RetryPolicy(maximum_attempts=1)), so a single sandbox failure lands in mark_review_failed (temporal/workflow.py:112-127, activities.py:820-846), which sets B FAILED, posts nothing to the PR, and leaves A COMPLETED. A later receiver refire (review_hog/backend/receivers.py:85-140, fires on TaskRun output saves carrying pr_url) then hits the dedupe, sees A, and does not recreate B, defeating the recovery the code explicitly designs for FAILED runs (test_tasks.py:970-1021 'failed_run_recreated_on_refire' docstring: 'a single-commit PR whose one review died isn't permanently stranded without a verdict'). Existing tests cover a lone COMPLETED or a lone FAILED run at the head, never both. Consequence is fail-safe: no approval stands over the unreviewed diff (A's was dismissed by B's startup sweep), the PR just stays unreviewed until the next push, another close/reopen, or a retarget; the 'existing_status=completed' log is the only wrong-status surface. Reachability needs a same-head re-review of a self-driving PR (reopen or retarget, uncommon), that re-review failing, and a subsequent output-save refire, which is itself opportunistic rather than a guaranteed retry. Human PRs never enter this path (the receiver leg is inbox-only).
notes: Would drop to not-real if _inbox_rereview_carve_out excluded 'reopened' and base retargets (then no same-head run B could follow a COMPLETED A for an inbox PR), or if mark_review_failed re-queued a replacement itself. Would rise to should_fix if TaskRun output saves routinely refire after the PR is open (making the refire the primary FAILED recovery in practice) or if reopen/retarget of self-driving PRs is common in the inbox flow. The suggested fix is small and correct: take the newest run at the head regardless of status, restart it when QUEUED, return early when live or delivered, and create a replacement when it is FAILED or SUPERSEDED; the equivalent same-head exclusion in _peer_persisted_approval_ids (activities.py:548) is a different concern and needs no change.
